messages:
lucy: quick RFC follow-up — I want to lock the interface direction for Hosted/Dedicated/Private capability negotiation. small thread to capture choices and rollout plan.

devin: tl;dr: prefer a single discovery pattern we can test in e2e harness. do we want probe endpoint or static manifest?

maria: +1 on single pattern. my leaning: static manifest delivered at install for Private (air-gapped), probe endpoint for Hosted/Dedicated where network is fine. keep both supported but with clear precedence.

ashok: we can support both. suggested precedence: 1) local manifest present -> use it, 2) call /internal/capabilities -> fallback, 3) default conservative feature set. manifest avoids outbound requirement for private. probe allows dynamic capability rollout for hosted.

lucy: that matches my mental model. tradeoffs to call out:
- manifest: easier for offline, but higher config drift risk and more operator burden.
- probe: simpler ops for hosted, but needs auth and increases surface area (network calls + ACLs).

devin: question: how do we represent capabilities? boolean flags? versions? we should avoid boolean explosion.

maria: prefer small typed descriptors with semantic versioning. e.g. capability name + minSupported + optional params. keeps negotiation stable.

devin: sample manifest snippet:
```
capabilities:
  - name: streaming_v2
    min_version: "2.0"
  - name: kv_cache
    min_version: "1.1"
    params: { max_prefix: 256 }
```

ashok: nice. operational notes: probe endpoint must require a signed ephemeral token (k8s service account or control-plane-issued) and rate-limited. logs only at info/debug to avoid leaking tenant topology.

lucy: call out incompatibilities: KMS-integrations and HSM-backed ops are hosted/dedicated features that Private might not support. we should surface these as capability flags so the client library can gracefully degrade (e.g., use local encryption fallback).

maria: +1. also add a capability "kms_external" with params describing key types. that will help SDKs pick fallbacks.

devin: rollout plan proposal:
1) spec v1 (manifest + probe) + capability schema + examples.
2) SDK change: read manifest -> fallback to probe. return capability object in client init.
3) implement in runtime: gate features behind capability checks; add telemetry events when a capability is missing.
4) start canary on hosted (5% traffic) and a dedicated cluster.

lucy: migration notes: we need a compatibility-mode for older runtimes. default to conservative: assume only core generation + embeddings. Add a header `X-Rw-Capabilities: opt-in=v1` so older runtimes ignore.

ashok: testing: add fake-adapter in e2e that can flip capabilities per-test. also add an offline manifest test for private installer.

maria: ops checklist before canary: update deploy manifests, create PKI tokens for probe auth, update docs + examples in quickstart. I'll own docs.

devin: small perf concern: clients should cache capabilities for reasonable TTL (5m by default). avoid probing on every request.

lucy: agreed. also add a warning in logs if capabilities changed mid-run (possible config drift).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary job queued -> architecture-runtime/capability-probe -> job id 2026-09-14-88.

maria: thanks, will open the follow-up PR for the spec and a short RFC diff. tagging @devin @ashok for review. :+1:

devin: will review. one last ask: add a compatibility matrix in the spec with explicit host/dedicated/private rows so integrators can scan quickly.

lucy: good call. I'll draft the matrix in the PR. closing notes: prefer interface-first (schema + auth) and keep implementation flexible. short and actionable. :rocket:
